Subject: Proposed temporary EU credit framework (draft)

Team — looping you in with the external request from Clearline. Below is the draft language I plan to propose; please review for legal/ops constraints. I attached a PDF with tracked changes and our maintenance calendar spreadsheet.

Draft proposal (high level):
- Scope: Applies to Redwood-hosted services for Clearline Health provisioned in the EU region only (region-scoped incidents). Global incidents remain subject to standard SLA language.
- Temporary uptime floor for May 2026: 99.5% (standard: 99.9%). This is timeboxed to the period 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-31, after which standard terms resume unless amended.
- Credit calculation: For region-scoped downtime, monthly credit = min( monthly_invoice * 0.30, monthly_invoice * (committed_uptime - achieved_uptime) / committed_uptime ). In plain terms: we cap credits at 30% of the monthly invoice and prorate based on the uptime shortfall.
- Planned maintenance carve-out: Maintenance listed in the agreed maintenance_schedule_2026Q2.xlsx (attached) is excluded from credit calculations if Redwood provides at least 72 hours' notice and publishes a post-maintenance summary within 72 hours of completion. Unscheduled maintenance or maintenance outside the agreed calendar will not be excluded.
- Operational commitments in the amendment: 72-hour postmortem for significant region-scoped incidents (>30m), targeted remediation steps, and a 30-day rollback window for Clearline to request configuration adjustments without penalty.

Attachments: proposed_sla_amendment_v2.pdf, maintenance_schedule_2026Q2.xlsx

Notes / asks:
- Dylan: confirm the 72-hour postmortem SLA is operationally feasible and whether we need to commit to an incident severity definition.
- Marissa: request quick legal check on the 30% cap and the rollback clause.

If both approve, I will send this to Samantha and procurement with a clean one-page amendment and a DocuSign link.

Thanks — Avery

2) Keep the credit cap but set the absolute cap at 30% of the monthly invoice (we have that). Add a minimum notice requirement for invoking the rollback window (14 days).
3) Add a requirement that Clearline acknowledge receipt of the maintenance calendar email (read receipt or reply) to qualify for the planned maintenance carve-out.
4) Add a short clause: Redwood will not apply credits to invoices already finalized and paid until a remediation reconciliation is completed — to avoid bookkeeping churn.
